Subject: Q3 capacity alignment + isolation confirmation

Hi Jasper / Aisha —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Below is a concise recap from our call so we have shared alignment and clear next steps. Please flag anything I mis-stated.

Quick summary (what you told us)
- Primary pain: unpredictable latency and noisy neighbors during model training/large-batch scoring windows; current multi-tenant provider sometimes reclaims resources mid-job.
- Constraint: PHI in inference payloads — NovaGen requires HIPAA controls, customer-specific isolation, and KMS-backed key management.
- Goals: 1) predictable throughput for clinical scoring pipelines, 2) secure per-tenant isolation, 3) ability to burst for nightly batches, 4) cost predictability for budgeting.
- Target SLOs you asked for: p95 generation latency < 200ms for small models (seq len ~512), p99 < 450ms; availability target ~99.9% for production routes.

What we propose (high-level)
- Reserved GPU pool: baseline of 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs dedicated to NovaGen (single-tenant pool).
- Burst policy: autoscale policy to allow temporary burst to 16 GPUs during scheduled batch windows (pre-agreed windows to guarantee capacity).
- Isolation options: dedicated tenant pool (software isolation + dedicated GPUs) or full VPC/private deployment (for stricter network isolation).
- Security: encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS, audit logs + access controls.

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA)
- Draft SOW + pricing ballpark (Camila / Dylan) — deliver draft by Tue, Oct 19.
- Deep technical session with SE to validate network/KMS details (Marissa) — propose Wed, Oct 20, 10:00am PT.
- Security evidence pack (SOC2 snippets, encryption docs) attached for procurement review — sending now.

Attachments included: redwood_reserved_gpu_proposal_Q3.pdf (high-level pricing + option combos), security-evidence-summary.zip (SOC2 excerpt, KMS notes), sow-draft-Novagen.docx (starter SOW).

Proposed pilot: 3-month reserved pool (8 GPUs) to validate latency and isolation before converting to annual reserved commitment.

Please confirm: (1) that the pilot cadence looks right, (2) whether you prefer dedicated pool or VPC option for the pilot, and (3) whether Oct 20 at 10am PT works for the SE call.

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly.

--
Camila Reyes

Hi Camila —

Thanks for the clear recap. This matches our notes and is helpful. A few clarifying questions before we lock in the SE call:

1) For the dedicated pool option, is isolation achieved at the hypervisor/instance level (i.e., hardware-allocated GPUs per tenant) or is it still a multi-tenant runtime with scheduling guarantees? We need to understand the failure modes for long-running batch scoring.

2) KMS: we run customer-managed keys (AWS KMS). Does Redwood support a bring-your-own-KMS model for the private deployment or hosted dedicated pools? We need key control for PHI.

3) Pricing: can you share a ballpark monthly committed price for the 8-GPU pilot and for the 12-month reserved? Our procurement timeline is tight — aiming to have a PO signed by Nov 15 if numbers look reasonable.

If you can include those answers in the SOW draft that would be great. Oct 20 at 10am PT works for the SE session for my team.

-Jasper

Hi Jasper / Aisha —

Appreciate the quick reply and the procurement timeline context. Short answers up front, full details attached and in the SOW draft.

1) Isolation model — options- a) Dedicated GPU pool (recommended pilot): GPUs physically dedicated to your tenant and scheduled by Redwood's tenant-aware runtime. This provides hardware-level isolation for GPU resources (no noisy neighbor GPU stealing during a job).- b) Private deployment (VPC / on-prem): full network & control-plane isolation with customer-managed networking and KMS — recommended if you want customer-controlled network egress rules and single-tenant control plane.

2) BYOK / KMS- Yes — we support BYOK for private deployments and for our dedicated pools via an integration with your AWS KMS. Keys are customer-controlled; Redwood never stores plaintext, and audit logs are available for key usage.

3) Ballpark pricing (high level) — final numbers in attached proposal / SOW:
- 3-month pilot (8 GPUs, burst to 16 allowed during scheduled windows): $68,000 / month (list) — estimated unit economics allow a ~15% discount for pilot.
- 12-month reserved (8 GPUs): $55,000 / month (committed annual rate).
- 12-month reserved + burst (allowing scheduled burst to 16): $66,000 / month with a negotiated burst allocation policy.

Notes: pricing includes runtime, autoscaling policy configuration, basic onboarding, and standard monitoring. Enterprise SLA (99.9%) and professional services for validation are add-ons in the SOW.

Next steps we propose:
- Camila to attach SOW draft and security evidence pack — attached here.
- Sign pilot SOW (DocuSign link below) to start provisioning: https://docusign.com/Envelope/ABC123
- SE deep-dive (Marissa) scheduled for Oct 20 10:00am PT to validate KMS flow and test cases.

Thanks — let me know if you want the pricing broken down to a per-GPU effective cost or tomography on observability/alerting for the p95/p99 latency SLOs.
